transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-04
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood Solutions), Ethan Cole (TideGate CTO), Priya Raman (TideGate Head of Security), Jonas Holt (Platform Eng), Asha Patel (Legal)

Summary: quick intake to understand TideGate's security constraints for choosing between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus on KMS/encryption, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and retention. Customer wants data residency and auditability for regulated financial telemetry.

Topics: SOC2/ISO certs, SAML/SSO integration patterns, KMS/HSM keys, RBAC and multi-tenant isolation, audit log retention and SIEM export, encryption at rest vs in transit, private deployment network topology, fallback strategies.

Action items: see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya, account lead for TideGate. We're joined by Rafael and Lina from our technical team. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Ethan Cole (TideGate CTO): Good, thanks. Busy but good. We wanted to, uh, use this call to get, like, the security constraints ironed out so our legal and infra teams can compare options.
00:14 Priya Raman (Head of Security): Yep. Main things for us are SOC2 or ISO evidence, SAML SSO, integration with our KMS, and clear audit logs we can ship to Splunk. Also data retention — we have different retention windows for PII vs telemetry.
00:25 Maya Chen: Great, that's exactly the scope. Rafael, do you want to start with how Redwood handles keys and encryption?
00:30 Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE): Sure — quick overview. For Hosted we use our multi-tenant key management where customer data is encrypted at rest with per-customer keys; for Dedicated we can integrate with customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault. For Private we support a bring-your-own-HSM pattern and can run customer-managed key material behind their VPC.
00:52 Jonas Holt (Platform Eng): When you say "integrate with KMS" — do you support envelope encryption or do you expect us to do client-side? We need to know if plaintext tokens ever touch your control plane.
01:05 Rafael: Good question. In Hosted the control plane handles request routing but we store only encrypted blobs; we use envelope encryption by default so customer CMKs wrap the data keys. For Dedicated the runtime nodes can be configured to request decryption via a VPC endpoint to your KMS, so plaintext is never stored in control plane logs. There's, uh, occasional mislabel in our docs where KV cache becomes KV cash, sorry, docs team is fixing that.
01:28 Priya: OK, yeah, we need a strict assurance that decrypt ops happen only in customer-controlled network segments. Is that in writing?
01:35 Maya: We have a security runbook and deployment diagrams — we'll share the private deployment topology showing where the decryption occurs. We'll also include a description of envelope flow. Rafael, add that to artifacts.
01:44 Rafael: Noted.
01:46 Asha Patel (Legal): On SOC2, do you have a timeline for certification? We need the Type II report or SOC2 equivalent for our procurement.
01:54 Maya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified — most recent report is Q3 2026. We also have ISO 27001 in progress, currently audited and pending final issuance. I'll attach the certs and the scope doc.
02:07 Priya: Do you have any exclusions? Like, is private deployment out of scope for SOC2?
02:12 Maya: The hosted service is covered. Private deployments are customer-managed; we provide an attestation of controls for the control plane but customers running on-prem will have their own audit scope. We'll include clarifying language.
02:24 Ethan: For SAML we use Okta — can you act as a SAML SP and support SCIM provisioning? We need group-based RBAC sync.
02:33 Rafael: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SP integration with IdPs including Okta, Azure AD, and OneLogin. SCIM for provisioning is supported on Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports SCIM for enterprise customers behind an enterprise tier. Group claims map to RBAC roles — we'll send a sample mapping file.
02:52 Jonas: Do you support attribute-based access control (ABAC) or is it only role-based? We have both fine-grained constraints and dynamic attributes.
03:01 Lina Park (Redwood Solutions): Currently RBAC is the default control surface — roles mapped to groups. We have ABAC features via our policy engine in Dedicated/Private deployments as an add-on; we can enable attribute tagging for tokens and resources. For Hosted, it's more conservative right now.
03:20 Priya: Audit logs — what's the retention and can we stream to our SIEM? We need immutable logs for 3 years for certain telemetry.
03:29 Rafael: Audit logs are retained by default 90 days in Hosted. For Dedicated we can configure retention — typical patterns: 90 days local, and long-term export to your S3 with lifecycle rules. For Private you control retention. We support streaming to Splunk, S3, or a Kafka endpoint. Immutable append-only logs are supported via WORM buckets on S3 if you need tamper evidence.
03:52 Ethan: Any cost associated with long-term log export?
03:55 Maya: There's a small egress/storage add-on for long-term retention in Hosted; for Dedicated it's typically included in the contract but depends on chosen retention. We'll put numbers in the pricing appendix.
04:06 Priya: Regarding data residency — can you pin instances to a EU region? We're regulated in EMEA.
04:11 Maya: Yes, we offer region pinning. Hosted has regional endpoints in EU and NA. Dedicated and Private allow you to deploy into specific cloud regions or on-prem clusters.
04:20 Asha: Legal question — do you process customer PII for model training? We need a guarantee of no training on customer data.
04:27 Rafael: Redwood does not use customer production data for model training unless there's an explicit opt-in. We'll provide a training policy.
04:33 Priya: Great. Also, can you redact or mask PII before tokenization? We want an inline sanitizer.
04:39 Lina: We provide pre-processing hooks and a sanitizer library customers can deploy. For Hosted we offer a managed PII scrub feature that can be enabled for enterprise customers.
04:51 Ethan: On fallback strategies: if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, can you route to Hosted temporarily? We need deterministic fallbacks for latency-sensitive flows.
04:59 Rafael: Yes — smart routing policies can route to a compatible model variant in Hosted or alternate Dedicated pool. You can set SLO-based fallback rules, cost thresholds, or hard blackouts. Note: when routing across tenancy boundaries, we respect encryption boundaries — we won't decrypt data in Hosted if keys are only in your Private KMS.
05:20 Priya: How do you surface auditability to our security ops? Do you provide immutable audit logs with user identifiers and API token usage?
05:27 Rafael: We instrument request tracing and token-level metadata. Audit logs include request id, user context, model variant, latency, and token counts. For customer-managed deployments we can inject your identity provider's identity attributes into logs.
05:40 Jonas: Small point — we need to ensure API keys are short-lived and integrate with our vault. Do you support short-lived tokens via STS?
05:47 Lina: Yes, we support short-lived credentials and STS-like flows, and integrations with HashiCorp Vault for secrets injection on Dedicated.
05:56 Asha: Procurement will want contract language around breach notifications and incident response SLA. What's the timeline for notification?
06:03 Maya: Our standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents and 24 hours for high-severity detection with an initial alert. We can negotiate different windows for enterprise contracts.
06:12 Priya: We also need proof of pen tests and vuln scanning cadence.
06:16 Rafael: We do annual third-party pen tests and monthly internal scans. We'll share the most recent pentest report redacted.
06:26 Ethan: How about data deletion and retention for things like logs created by the inference engine, e.g., prompts and completions? We have to delete PII on request within 30 days typically.
06:36 Rafael: For Hosted we have deletion APIs and a data retention config per customer — default is 90 days; we can set to 30 days for enterprise. For Dedicated/Private you control retention and deletion semantics. For Hosted we maintain deletion audit trails.
06:48 Priya: Who has access to those deletion logs internally? We need RBAC on admin actions.
06:53 Lina: Only authorized security ops with specific roles can perform deletion and view deletion logs; all admin actions are logged and require SSO enforced 2FA.
07:05 Ethan: About private deployment: what does the network topology look like? We want an air-gapped option for certain customers.
07:12 Rafael: Private on-prem can be air-gapped. We ship a control plane shim that runs in your environment and a minimal telemetry collector. For fully air-gapped setups, we do a manual onboarding and offline attestation process.
07:25 Jonas: Manual onboarding — does that add significant time?
07:28 Maya: Typically 6 to 12 weeks for full on-prem air-gapped deployment including security review and integration. Dedicated in cloud is faster — 2 to 4 weeks typically.
07:39 Priya: For compliance mapping, can you provide a matrix that maps Redwood controls to our SOC2+ISO requirements? That will save time for our audit team.
07:46 Maya: Absolutely — we'll include a control mapping matrix as part of the artefacts.
07:50 Asha: We use Splunk for log ingestion — is there a supported connector or do you recommend S3+lambda?
07:57 Rafael: We have a native Splunk HEC integration we can enable to stream audit logs; alternatively S3 export with lambda transform works fine. We'll put both patterns in the design doc.
08:08 Priya: Encryption in transit — TLS, perfect forward secrecy?
08:11 Rafael: TLS 1.3 with modern ciphers, yes. For inter-node traffic in Dedicated/Private you can opt into mutual TLS.
08:20 Ethan: Is there any piece of metadata you store forever? We want to know about long-lived identifiers.
08:25 Lina: We persist request IDs and anonymized usage aggregates for billing and quality monitoring; we can configure retention for raw request metadata. We don't retain raw prompt text longer than retention window unless customer opts in.
08:38 Priya: For legal holds, can you place a hold on deletion for specific datasets?
08:43 Rafael: We support legal hold flags on customer buckets in Dedicated/Private, and on Hosted we have a litigation hold process that freezes deletion until cleared. We'll provide the workflow.
08:56 Ethan: A bit of a tangent — are there any restrictions on using custom models? We want to bring a tuned model where weights are sensitive.
09:04 Rafael: You can bring your own model weights into Dedicated or Private. For Hosted we have model onboarding review and MLOps constraints; we don't accept private weights into multi-tenant Hosted runtime without encryption and legal review.
09:20 Priya: Regarding attestations, can we do a supplier security review and get references?
09:24 Maya: Yes, we can provide customer references and completed vendor questionnaires (SIG Lite, CAIQ). We'll send the completed docs.
09:32 Ethan: Ok practical next steps — we need pricing delta for Dedicated vs Hosted plus a sketch of architecture for Private. Also the SOC2 artefacts and SAML/SCIM mapping file.
09:43 Maya: We'll send a package: SOC2 + ISO status, KMS integration guide, SAML/SCIM mapping sample, audit log export patterns, and a first-pass architecture for Private with onboarding timeline. Rafael will run a Dedicated perf sample.
09:58 Priya: One last thing — do you have anomaly detection on admin actions? We want alerts on unusual deletion or key rotation.
10:05 Rafael: We have an admin-activity anomaly detection module that can hook into SIEM and send alerts; we'll include configuration notes.
10:13 Asha: For contract language, we'll want indemnity carveouts around customer data. We'll circulate redlines after we get SOC2.
10:20 Maya: Understood.
10:22 Ethan: Thanks. We'll review the artifacts and schedule the technical deep-dive with your SE for the week of Feb 8.
10:27 Maya: Great. Thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and set up the next call.

[End of recording]

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mislabels (Speaker 3 shows as "Speaker 4" in sections), some technical terms transcribed oddly ("KV cache" as "K V cash"), and punctuation is imperfect.
